title: Capitalise Each Word
statement:
Title-case a line: the first letter of each word upper-case, every other letter lower-case.

## Your function

```
std::string Capitalise(std::string text);
```

A *word* starts at any character that follows a space (or at the start of the string). Spaces are kept exactly as given -- including runs of several and leading or trailing ones. Characters that are not letters are left as they are.

```
"hELLO wORLD"   ->  "Hello World"
"  a  b "       ->  "  A  B "
```

## Watch out

- **`text` is taken by value, so you may modify it and return it.** No second string is needed.
- **Track "start of a word" with a flag**, not by looking at `text[i - 1]` for `i == 0`.
- **Cast to `unsigned char`** before `std::toupper` / `std::tolower`; a negative `char` is undefined behaviour.
- Do not use `split` / `istringstream`: they collapse the spaces, and the spaces must survive.

tests.name: leading, repeated and trailing spaces are preserved
tests.description: The output is bracketed so the spaces are visible.

tests.name: non-letters are left alone
tests.description: '3d-printing' becomes '3d-printing'; the 'd' follows a digit, not a space.
